items.headline: Three Iran-backed suspects plotted attacks including RAF Fairford incident, US says
items.blurb: The US Department of Justice says the men were involved in a string of plots, including a major incident near the UK airbase that is used by US armed forces.
items.text: The US Department of Justice (DOJ) has announced charges against three Iran-backed operatives that it alleges were involved in a string of plots in the US and Europe. The DOJ said Iranian agents most recently "orchestrated a terrorist plot at an air force base in the United Kingdom", saying they were involved in the major incident in September near RAF Fairford in the UK, where US armed forces were stationed. One man, a dual Iranian-Iraqi national, is accused of communicating with contacts in the UK from a prison in New York where he is awaiting trial on previous charges. The other two are accused of doing the same from Iran. Iran has strongly denied any involvement in the RAF Fairford incident, which came to light when suspicious vans were reported near the base. Seven men have been arrested in the UK over the incident. Iranian Mohsen Mohajeri, Iraqi national Mohammad Ali al-Hassani and dual Iranian-Iraqi citizen Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi were charged in an indictment unsealed on Tuesday, the DOJ said. items.headline: US Army soldier suspected of spying for Russia arrested in UK
items.blurb: The 41-year-old senior soldier is accused of national security offences and is being questioned in London.
items.text: A soldier in the US Army has been arrested on suspicion of spying for Russia, British counter-terror police have said. Counter Terrorism Policing London said the man had been arrested under section one and section three of the National Security Act 2023. Section one of the Act relates to obtaining or disclosing protected information, while section three relates to assisting a foreign intelligence service. As part of the investigation, officers are carrying out searches at two locations in Gloucestershire. The BBC understands the soldier was based at Imjin Barracks in Innsworth, Gloucestershire. The barracks serve as the headquarters of Nato's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps (ARRC) , a strategic operational base for the alliance. Counter Terrorism Policing said it was not linked to any other ongoing investigations. FBI director Kash Patel said in a statement: "This important arrest involves allegations of espionage, which is of the utmost concern to the United States and our allies." items.headline: Collision of two trains in Egypt kills at least seven
items.blurb: President orders prompt investigation after one train derails in collision in al-Ayyat about 50km from Cairo Seven people were killed and at least 125 injured when two trains collided on Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, officials said.
items.text: President orders prompt investigation after one train derails in collision in al-Ayyat about 50km from Cairo Seven people were killed and at least 125 injured when two trains collided on Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, officials said. The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 50km (30 miles) south of Cairo, when a train travelling to Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the transport ministry. An inspection indicated that the Cairo-Aswan train had been stationary on the same track, officials said. The health ministry gave the casualty toll, adding more than 70 of the injured were discharged after receiving treatment. Train derailments and crashes are common in Egypt, where the railway system has a history of mismanagement and poor maintenance of equipment. In recent years the government has announced modernisation initiatives to improve its railways. items.blurb: Trump welcomes the outcome, praising Hegseth as a "Great American Patriot", but Democrats can try again next year.
items.text: An effort to impeach US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, accusing him of waging war on Iran without congressional authorisation, has failed on Capitol Hill. A majority of the House of Representatives agreed to refer impeachment articles to a committee - essentially killing the effort introduced by dissident Republican congressman Thomas Massie of Kentucky - for now. In his first news briefing from the Pentagon in six months, Hegseth called the impeachment effort a "farce" and "sabotage". The bid to find the cabinet secretary guilty of misconduct and ultimately remove him from office was seen as a long shot as it could have required a number of other Republicans to defy President Donald Trump. Massie was the only Republican to vote against moving the resolution to the Republican-led House Judiciary Committee on Tuesday. His effort failed in a 211–204 vote, with more than a dozen members, including 11 Democrats, missing the vote. items.blurb: The men, including one who is already in jail, face charges over alleged plot at UK air base used in US war on Iran.
items.text: US indicts three men over alleged 'terror' attacks in US and Europe, including UK air base plot Prosecutors in the United States have charged three men they describe as Iranian-backed operatives over their alleged role in nearly 20 attacks and attempted attacks across the US and Europe, including a plot targeting the United Kingdom’s Fairford air base . The Department of Justice said on Tuesday that the three men acted in support of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and Iraq’s Kataib Hezbollah. It identified the men as Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi, Mohsen Mohajeri and Mohammad Ali al-Hassani, who face what it called “terrorism-related offenses”. Al-Saadi is already in jail in New York. Prosecutors did not disclose the whereabouts of Mohajeri and al-Hassani. The charges announced on Tuesday centre on RAF Fairford in southwest England, where US forces and bombers had been stationed. The US had used the base to deploy bombers in its war against Iran. The festival is part of See My World’s year-round programme showcasing pan-African arts, culture and events. items.headline: Meghan's father Thomas Markle back in federal custody after allegedly removing ankle monitor
items.blurb: The 82-year-old was placed under house detention in Florida last week after being charged over possession of child sex abuse material.
items.text: Thomas Markle, the father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, is back in federal custody in Florida after allegedly removing his ankle monitor, according to court documents. Markle appeared before a federal magistrate judge in the Florida city of Tampa on Tuesday and was denied bond. Prosecutors say he removed the monitor early that morning. US Judge Lindsay S Griffin found on Tuesday that Markle had violated the conditions of his pretrial release, court documents show. Markle, who has denied possessing images of child sex abuse, was arrested in Florida last week and placed under house detention. He was also ordered to wear a location monitoring device. Griffin described Markle's housing situation as "untenable", writing in the order revoking his pretrial release that "based on the lack of suitable housing, no condition or combination of conditions would reasonably assure the safety of any other person or the community and the defendant's appearance in court". items.headline: Over 74 lakh voters missing from Tamil Nadu electoral rolls, says citizens’ collective
items.blurb: The collective has announced a rally on Anna Salai on November 26, as part of a nationwide day of action against the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls
items.text: Political economist Parakala Prabhakar speaking at a press conference in Chennai on Tuesday. Carnatic vocalist T.M. Krishna and IYCC co-convenor Radhika Ganesh are also seen. | Photo Credit: R. RAGU The Independent Young Citizens Collective (IYCC) has alleged that 74.07 lakh voters have been removed from Tamil Nadu’s electoral rolls and demanded an inquiry into the alleged deletions. Announcing a rally on Anna Salai on November 26, as part of a nationwide day of action against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, the collective said the reported deletion of such a large number of names has raised serious questions about the exercise and its implications for democracy. The IYCC is part of ‘People Against SIR’, a national platform comprising mass organisations, social movements and individual activists, independent of political parties. The collective released its statement at a press conference at the Chennai Press Club on Tuesday. items.blurb: Navtej SarnaOn the landscape of our discontent, several craters pose immediate challenges: Conflicts without end, struggling multilateral institutions, trade handcuffed by tariffs, the looming AI takeover, and so on
items.text: On the landscape of our discontent, several craters pose immediate challenges: Conflicts without end, struggling multilateral institutions, trade handcuffed by tariffs, the looming AI takeover, and so on. It is easy, and often profitable, to turn one’s face away from the challenge of climate change. Performative grandstanding – as we will no doubt see at COP 31 in Antalya, Turkey — or superficial greenwashing is considered sufficient. This deliberate downplaying or ignoring of the climate crisis now has a name: Climate hushing. But monsters don’t go away with a finger on their lips. While the world is looking elsewhere, the Earth’s climate system is hurtling headlong into uncharted waters. Several vital markers of the climate crisis are at record extremes: Carbon dioxide levels are higher now than at any time in the last two million years; extreme heat, droughts, floods and wildfires are common occurrences; glacier thickness and Greenland ice mass are at record lows. items.text: A day after the Acting Foreign Minister of Bangladesh, Humayun Kabir, stressed that Dhaka would not issue a passport to deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina and insisted on getting her extradited from India under an “acceptable prisoner exchange”, the Ministry of External Affairs said on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) that a “travel document” was needed for international travel. “Extradition of former Prime Minister of Bangladesh Sheikh Hasina is a legal matter and it will be dealt with accordingly,” said Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal in response to a question about Ms. Hasina’s presence in India. He described the passport’s requirement for extradition as a “technical issue” and said, “Obviously, for the travel of people, you need a travel document.” Officials said Ms. Hasina can be extradited either on a Bangladeshi passport or an Emergency Certificate that would prove that she has Bangladeshi citizenship. items.text: New Delhi reacted strongly on Tuesday to reports of Chinese influencers filming videos in Bangladesh and passing them off as depictions of India, calling on authorities in Beijing and Dhaka to take action against those involved in presenting a “distorted picture” of the country. Reports in the Bangladesh media said scores of Chinese vloggers and influencers were involved in a campaign of shooting videos in the impoverished neighbourhoods of Uttara and Tekpara in Dhaka and passing off their broadcasts as originating in New Delhi. “We have seen media reports in this regard. Such efforts to present a distorted picture of any country are unfortunate,” external affairs ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said when he was asked about the activities of Chinese influencers in Dhaka. “Insofar as efforts by foreign elements to portray parts of Dhaka as Delhi are concerned, peddling of false narratives only undermines the credibility of those who are undertaking such actions and those who are behind them. items.text: US-Iran war : US President Donald Trump's remarks that the Iran war is "effectively over" have raised hopes of easing geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, potentially providing relief to global financial markets. The comments could influence investor sentiment towards riskier assets such as equities while also triggering volatility in traditional safe-haven investments such as gold and silver. For Indian markets, any signs of de-escalation between the US and Iran could be positive, particularly if they lead to a sustained decline in crude oil prices. Lower oil prices could ease India's imported inflation concerns, support the rupee and improve the outlook for corporate earnings. However, the impact on precious metals could be more complicated. While easing inflation concerns and expectations of lower interest rates could support bullion prices, a reduction in geopolitical uncertainty could also reduce demand for gold and silver as safe-haven assets. According to market experts, Trump's remarks could provide a near-term boost to Indian equities by easing geopolitical uncertainty and improving global risk appetite. items.text: Poundland and its 11,000 employees are hopeful that the retailer's impending collapse can be delayed to allow time for a last-minute rescue deal. The discount chain has been edging towards administration after being blocked by its owners from accessing cash in its bank accounts. A deadline to secure a buyer for the business is set to expire at midnight, but sources close to the situation have told the BBC that they expect more time will be given, thanks to the release of £10m in funding. A committee of MPs is set to question Gordon Brothers, Poundland's US owners, on Wednesday following accusations that the investment firm hopes to profit from selling off Poundland's 600 stores and stock piecemeal. Gordon Brothers - which bought the chain for just £1 last year - is accused of forcing that outcome by restricting Poundland's access to available cash needed to restock stores and pay wages and rent, ahead of the crucial Christmas trading period. items.blurb: Inside ShareChat’s Mixed FY26 ShareChat parent Mohalla Tech delivered some hits and some misses in FY26. While the homegrown social…
items.text: ShareChat parent Mohalla Tech delivered some hits and some misses in FY26. While the homegrown social media giant crossed the ₹1,000 Cr revenue mark and found a new growth engine in microdramas, what played the spoilsport were losses and surging expenses. Loss Widens: Mohalla Tech’s FY26 losses were largely driven by rising expenses. Employee benefit costs more than doubled YoY in the fiscal under review, while forex losses also surged following Rupee’s depreciation. Meanwhile, marketing and user acquisition spending also jumped nearly 8X YoY as Mohalla Tech invested aggressively in growth. The Microdrama Pivot: The launch of QuickTV opened a crucial new revenue stream and generated nearly a third of Mohalla Tech’s total income in FY26. items.text: Grok Build, the vibe-coding agent from SpaceXSI, is leaking data—some of it proprietary business information and other sensitive secrets—from thousands of its users, including the very same Elon Musk-owned company that offers the platform, new research shows. The information is revealed through links allowing Grok Build users to share their apps with others. Grok takes steps to randomize the URLs so only people who know the exact URL can access the data stored there. A design decision by developers of the platform, however, completely torpedoes that objective and makes it possible for anyone to enumerate thousands of live Grok Build projects. Except in rare cases, clicking those links opens the app and reveals all data associated with it. Research from security firm Claroc shows that the exposed data includes things like internal business plans, ad proposals, medical exam results, galley checklists from a celebrity cruise line, and employee names and ID numbers. items.headline: DeepMind reveals Gemini Robotics 2.5 and open safety benchmark "ASIMOV-jailbreak"
items.blurb: The new model is up to twice as successful at some tasks.
items.text: Google DeepMind has revealed a new generation of the AI-powered Gemini Robotics platform. In the 2.5 release, Google says its robotic AI is getting tantalizingly close to completing real-world tasks as well as humans do. In fact, some Gemini robots were able to get actual work done in Mercedes-Benz factories, and the team is preparing for a day when robots operate alongside humans with an open source safety benchmark. DeepMind’s physical AI platform has several computational layers between user input and robotic action. There’s the vision-language model piece, which is Gemini Embodied Reasoning. Essentially, it takes your instructions and uses live video to plan how the robot can accomplish the task. The other main component is the vision-language-action (VLA) that actually generates robot actions, like moving an actuator—that’s Gemini Robotics, which has been bumped to version 2.5. DeepMind says that Gemini Robotics 2.5 is much better at tasks that require a high degree of dexterity. The model was evaluated across more than 200 activities, including serving food with tongs and using a pipette, as you would see in a laboratory.

items.headline: What happens to mathematics when AI becomes an oracle?
items.blurb: Mathematician Steven Strogatz discusses his new book, Big Math: The Hidden Codes That Run Our World .
items.text: Our modern world runs on math, from social media algorithms, package delivery, and weather prediction to medical imaging and machine learning. The rise of computers helped fuel its dominance, enabling us to work with increasingly large numbers that would otherwise be beyond the capacity of our finite human brains. But with the rise of large language models, AI chatbots, and, soon, quantum computing, so-called “big math” is beginning to outstrip its creators entirely. What that means , and how we might adapt, is the focus of a new book, Big Math: The Hidden Codes That Run Our World , by applied mathematicians Steven Strogatz and Alex Townsend. Strogatz is perhaps best known in his field for his co-authorship of a seminal 1998 paper with Duncan Watts on the collective dynamics of small-world networks. He has also studied chaos theory as applied to physics, the geometry of supercoiled DNA, and the biological collective oscillators, such as swarms of synchronously flashing fireflies and crickets that chirp in unison. items.text: Impervious to battlefield jamming, drones physically connected to human operators by miles of fiber-optic cables have become such a common weapon of war in Ukraine that trees and fields are strewn with tangled cables thinner than fishing lines. But importing such fiber-optic material from China has become more costly as drone warfare’s needs compete with global demand from AI data centers for the same limited supply—and so Ukrainian drone makers have been adapting. Since the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine began in February 2022, the Ukrainians have been forced out of necessity to continually develop battlefield innovations involving first-person view (FPV) quadcopter drones and other heavier types of drones. But it was the Russian military that first deployed unjammable fiber-optic drones to repel Ukrainian forces’ cross-border incursion into the Kursk Oblast in 2024. The Ukrainians quickly followed suit in developing their own fiber-optic drones, given the drones’ capability to shrug off electronic warfare jamming that could neutralize radio-controlled drones. items.text: New York is gearing up to enforce one of the country’s most significant AI safety laws. The state opened a registration portal Tuesday, with which large frontier AI developers like Anthropic and OpenAI will be required to register by January 1, 2027. The RAISE Act , New York’s safety and transparency bill, kicks in at the start of the year. It mandates that large frontier developers — companies with more than $500 million in annual revenue — have to publish safety frameworks on their websites, report critical safety incidents within 72 hours, and issue public model transparency reports. The newly formed Office of Digital Innovation, Governance, Integrity, and Trust (DIGIT) will implement the RAISE Act and oversee large frontier AI labs. Penalties can be as high as $1 million for one violation and $3 million for subsequent violations. Francis is a proven founder who has built multiple businesses to help people travel, and we’re excited he’s chosen to build with us.” However the AI lab has not announced new travel-specific products or plans. It does, however, count such companies as Bookings.com, Expedia, and KAYAK as customers or partners.

items.blurb: Each of the seven co-founders plans to sell exactly the same number of shares in the IPO, which would bring each of them about $250 million in cash at the midpoint of the price range while leaving the group in control of the company.
items.text: As Anthropic barrels toward an enormous IPO that could value it at $1.4 trillion, the company has disclosed a tidbit in its new S-1 filing about how many shares each of its seven co-founders plan to sell. Each will sell 3,378,378 shares. Anthropic has floated an unusually broad initial price range of $70 to $78 a share. At the midrange of $74, each founder would take in just shy of $250 million. At the low end, $70, each would have to settle for pocketing just over $236 million in cash; at the high end, $78, each would take in just under $264 million. However, in an IPO as eagerly anticipated as this one, companies can often price shares above the initial range. The S-1 is already hinting at high demand. items.text: Oura announced on Tuesday that it’s acquiring AI-native primary care company Counsel Health for $625 million. The deal comes a few weeks after Oura postponed its up to $2.2 billion IPO indefinitely, citing “uncertainty in the IPO market.” Counsel Health is an AI-powered healthcare platform that combines a chat-based medical experience with access to licensed physicians. Its service was integrated into the Oura app in June. Users can connect with Counsel’s medical AI to get personalized medical advice, and chat with a physician when needed, all within the Oura app. Now, the companies plan to expand on their existing partnership to build across preventative care, acute care, and specialty and chronic care. items.text: A selloff in US-listed neoclouds and growing scrutiny of NVIDIA have raised questions about the financing model underpinning the AI infrastructure boom, with potential implications for India's GPU cloud providers. Unlike their US peers, backed by large hyperscaler customers, Indian neoclouds have only limited domestic anchor demand and rely on international customers, government-backed compute requirements and evolving financing arrangements to fund expansion. As NVIDIA’s influence extends beyond GPU supply to financing and strategic partnerships, Indian players face questions around debt exposure, customer commitments, GPU depreciation and whether their infrastructure investments can withstand a global market correction. The alleged espionage scandal involving NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang and the growing scrutiny of the chipmaker’s business dealings with China have added another layer of uncertainty to the global AI infrastructure market already facing questions about its financing model. At the same time, political and regulatory resistance to data centre expansion in the US could slow infrastructure investment, putting pressure on companies that have borrowed heavily to build capacity. The support also includes $200K in Google Cloud credits and pro bono technical expertise from Google’s AI specialists. The funding will help Froncort.AI develop mAI-NETRA, a mobile version of its public health platform AI-NETRA, which uses AI, satellite imagery and government health data to identify higher risk areas for catching infectious diseases. It also guides frontline health workers towards targeted screenings. The startup is among 15 organisations selected globally for Google.org’s Impact Challenge: AI for Government Innovation. items.headline: OpenAI Deploys Control Room With 35-Second Kill Switch Amid Security Concerns
items.blurb: Amid growing threats of rogue AI agents, ChatGPT parent OpenAI has developed and deployed Control Room, a centralised system to…
items.text: OpenAI has introduced Control Room, a centralised system that can halt AI model output within 35 seconds of a decision to intervene The system aims to contain potentially unsafe AI behaviour as autonomous agents face growing scrutiny over their ability to act beyond intended instructions Control Room works with OpenAI's misalignment monitoring systems, checks research jobs through unique IDs and blocks inference requests if a job is terminated or the system becomes unavailable Amid growing threats of rogue AI agents, ChatGPT parent OpenAI has developed and deployed Control Room, a centralised system to monitor its AI research workloads and stop models from generating output within 35 seconds of a decision to intervene. In a blog post, the company noted that all advanced AI training jobs are monitored by a separate AI model that flags potentially problematic behaviour. If an issue is detected, the monitoring system can instruct the Control Room to terminate the job.
